test_title: PYST 37: SSC GD Constable 2025 - General Knowledge (Held On: 21 Feb, 2025 - Shift 1)

question: Which of the following is NOT considered a Fundamental Right under the Indian Constitution?
solution:
The correct answer is __**4) Right to Property**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Right to Property** was originally a Fundamental Right under Article 31 of the Constitution of India.
 
• It was removed from the list of Fundamental Rights by the 44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978, and made a **legal right** under Article 300A.
 
• Fundamental Rights are guaranteed under Part III of the Constitution, but the Right to Property is not included in this category anymore.
 
• The Right to Property, as a legal right, ensures that no person shall be deprived of their property except by the authority of law.
 
• Unlike Fundamental Rights, a legal right under Article 300A is not enforceable directly in the Supreme Court under Article 32.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fundamental Rights in India:**

 
 
• There are six Fundamental Rights enshrined in the Indian Constitution, which are essential for the development of individuals and protecting them from state encroachment.
 
• These include the Right to Equality (Articles 14-18), Right to Freedom (Articles 19-22), Right against Exploitation (Articles 23-24), Right to Freedom of Religion (Articles 25-28), Cultural and Educational Rights (Articles 29-30), and Right to Constitutional Remedies (Article 32).
 
 
 
• **Legal Rights vs. Fundamental Rights:**
 
 
• Legal rights are granted by ordinary laws and can be amended or repealed by the legislature, whereas Fundamental Rights are enshrined in the Constitution and are protected from legislative encroachment.
 
• Fundamental Rights are enforceable by the Supreme Court under Article 32, but legal rights are enforceable in lower courts.
 
 
 
• **44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978:**
 
 
• This amendment abolished the Right to Property as a Fundamental Right and reclassified it as a constitutional legal right under Article 300A.
 
• The amendment was introduced to reduce conflicts between the state and individuals over property acquisition for public purposes.
 
 
 
• **Right to Property under Article 300A:**
 
 
• It ensures that no person shall be deprived of their property except by the authority of law, providing protection against arbitrary dispossession.
 
• However, since it is not a Fundamental Right, violations cannot be directly challenged in the Supreme Court under Article 32.
